name: Tampa
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Tampa: Florida-licensed investigator coordination, counterparty and asset research, defense diligence.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Tampa, scoped from Nashville: background and asset research on Florida companies and individuals, diligence on port, logistics and defense-contracting counterparties, and factual support for counsel in Florida state and federal litigation, with field work coordinated through investigators licensed under Florida law.
intro: Tampa is Florida's third-largest city, with an estimated 413,554 residents on 1 July 2025 according to the US Census Bureau, and anchors the Tampa-St. Petersburg-Clearwater metropolitan area of about 3.4 million people. The city describes its economy as resting on tourism, agriculture, construction, finance, health care, government and technology. The Port of Tampa is described by the city as Florida's largest port, and Tampa International Airport serves the region. MacDill Air Force Base in south Tampa employs about 19,000 people and hosts US Central Command and US Special Operations Command, which draws defense contractors and consultants to the area. The University of South Florida and the University of Tampa add research and professional services activity.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Tampa for reasons tied to this mix. Defense and government contractors clustered around MacDill need to understand subcontractors, teaming partners and foreign-linked suppliers. Port and logistics business brings bulk cargo, trade finance and supply chain questions. Rapid population growth and construction have produced real estate, development and insurance disputes, and Florida's attractiveness to relocating businesses and individuals means investors and creditors often need to trace people, companies and assets that have moved to the state. Financial services and healthcare employers also commission work on fraud, misconduct and litigation support.

matters.title: Defense contractor and supplier diligence
matters.text: Background research on subcontractors, teaming partners and suppliers serving commands at MacDill Air Force Base, covering ownership, foreign links, debarment and litigation history and adverse media, so primes and investors can assess integrity, conflict of interest and foreign ownership risks before awards or acquisitions.

matters.title: Port and trade counterparty research
matters.text: Researching importers, exporters, freight forwarders and commodity traders using the Port of Tampa, including ownership, corporate history, litigation and sanctions screening, to support lenders and buyers concerned about trade finance fraud, misdescribed cargo or counterparties with undisclosed foreign principals.

matters.title: Relocated individuals and asset tracing
matters.text: Locating lawfully documented property, company interests and judgments for creditors and counsel pursuing individuals or businesses that have relocated to the Tampa area, and identifying related entities, transfers and homestead or trust structures that counsel should examine before enforcement.

matters.title: Real estate and construction disputes
matters.text: Background and litigation research on developers, contractors, public adjusters and investors active in Hillsborough County, supporting counsel and insurers in construction defect, delay, insurance and investment disputes arising from the region's rapid growth and storm exposure.

matters.title: Executive and transaction backgrounds
matters.text: Pre-transaction and pre-hire research on executives, founders and companies based in Tampa Bay financial services, healthcare and technology, covering regulatory actions, litigation, bankruptcies, business affiliations and media, with findings reported under applicable consumer reporting rules where they apply.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Tampa
local_context.text: Tampa is the seat of Hillsborough County, whose state trial courts form part of Florida's Thirteenth Judicial Circuit, and of the Tampa Division of the US District Court for the Middle District of Florida, which also has a bankruptcy court in the city. Docket research across these courts, together with Pinellas and Pasco County courts nearby, is central to understanding a Tampa counterparty's litigation, foreclosure and bankruptcy history.

local_context.title: Florida investigator licensing
local_context.text: Florida licenses private investigators under Chapter 493 of the Florida Statutes, administered by the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services through its Division of Licensing. Individuals hold Class C licences, agencies Class A, and interns Class CC under sponsorship. Unlicensed private investigation is a criminal offence, and licensees may not disclose investigative files except to the client or as permitted. Attorneys and some other professionals are exempt.

local_context.title: Florida corporate and property records
local_context.text: Florida companies register with the Division of Corporations, whose public filings typically show officers or managers, registered agents and annual reports. Deeds, mortgages, liens and judgments in Hillsborough County are recorded with the county clerk, and property data is maintained by the property appraiser. These records are a starting point, but beneficial owners often sit behind Florida LLCs or out-of-state entities.

local_context.title: Defense and federal presence
local_context.text: MacDill Air Force Base hosts US Central Command and US Special Operations Command, making Tampa a hub for defense contracting, intelligence support and related consulting. Matters involving these companies may raise export control, security clearance and federal procurement integrity issues, so research is scoped carefully and stays within public, lawfully available information. Findings are reported with sources so clients can rely on them.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Tampa, TDSC first defines the question, whether that is a contractor's foreign links, a trader's reliability, a relocated debtor's assets or an executive's history, and then identifies the relevant Florida and federal records, including Hillsborough County filings, state corporate records and federal dockets. Desk research is conducted from Nashville. Because Florida requires a Chapter 493 licence for private investigation, any field work in Tampa, such as interviews or observation, is carried out by investigators licensed in Florida and coordinated by TDSC. Consumer report rules under the Fair Credit Reporting Act are applied where findings will inform employment or similar decisions, and work for litigation is directed by counsel.

faqs.q: Does Florida require a licence for investigative work in Tampa?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 493 of the Florida Statutes requires private investigators and agencies to be licensed by the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, subject to exemptions such as attorneys in practice. TDSC is based in Nashville; field work in Florida is coordinated through appropriately licensed Florida investigators, and our own role is research and consulting.

faqs.q: Can you trace assets of someone who has moved to the Tampa area?
faqs.a: We search lawfully available property, corporate, court, lien and judgment records in Hillsborough and neighbouring counties and in other states, and identify related entities and transfers. Florida's homestead and exemption rules can affect what is collectible, so findings are passed to counsel, who advise on enforcement.

faqs.q: Do you research defense contractors linked to MacDill?
faqs.a: Yes, within public and lawfully available sources: ownership, corporate history, federal contract and exclusion records, litigation and media. We look for undisclosed foreign ownership, conflicts of interest and integrity issues. We do not seek classified or restricted information, and we flag where a question requires the client's security or export control specialists.

faqs.q: Which courts should be checked for a Tampa counterparty?
faqs.a: Typically the Hillsborough County courts of the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit, the Tampa Division of the Middle District of Florida and the related bankruptcy court, plus nearby county courts and courts in states where the counterparty previously operated. Searching only one level or county can miss foreclosures, judgments and federal cases.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Tampa?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office or staff in Tampa. We conduct research and scope engagements from Nashville and, where Florida work requires it, coordinate investigators licensed under Florida law. We do not use pretexting or seek records obtainable only through restricted access.
